announcements.text: A cron job whose run is interrupted by an OpenCrabs daemon restart delivers its result to NO channel: boot revival resumes the turn with no job identity, run id or deliver_to, so the job output reaches nobody. Ship-chain hot-reloads make restarts frequent, so any factory relying on cron delivery is exposed.

vpn/services/gatus/config/config.yaml carries live credentials in plaintext, including SSH private-key blocks. Never grep it with a context flag (-A/-B), and never print a parsed form of it - json.dumps of a single endpoint dict renders the key field verbatim. Read the KEY NAMES only; to compare a value, hash it in place. The read discipline is necessary but not sufficient: the PRINT is the second chokepoint, and it is the one that fails when the read felt safe. A third chokepoint is any TOOL whose output path renders the file's content: a diff, a checksum-and-dump, or a guard that prints a drift diff between two key-bearing copies discloses both. Read the output path before you ship the tool, not after.

announcements.text: infra_mac-cdp-tunnel (endpoint_id 15) was RED for 20 h 18 min — Gatus's own event table reads UNHEALTHY 2026-10-23T10:05:09Z → HEALTHY 2026-10-24T06:23:09Z — and an earlier version of this entry read "110 results / 0 failures", true only of the window it was read in, four hours before the outage began. THE MECHANISM, read from the endpoint's own definition rather than inferred: it is NOT a Mac-localhost check. The URL is ssh://78.17.187.4:15259 — which `getent hosts` resolves to THIS host, agents — and the body then runs `curl -s --max-time 3 http://localhost:9222/json/version | grep -c Macintosh` ON AGENTS. `grep -c` exits 1 on zero matches, so the probe is red whenever nothing listens on agents' loopback:9222; the probed object is the FORWARDER, not the Mac. THE MAC WAS HEALTHY THROUGHOUT: with the endpoint red, `ssh mac` succeeded and CDP answered Chrome/150.0.7871.1016 with a Macintosh User-Agent. THE DEFECT WAS SUPERVISION, NOW CLOSED AND PROVEN ACROSS A REBOOT: the forwarder had been hand-launched every time, so it died and nothing brought it back. It is now a repo unit, agents/services/mac-cdp/mac-cdp-tunnel.service (vds-servers 6bd06c02), Restart=always with ServerAliveInterval 15 x3 — so ssh EXITS on a missed probe when the Mac sleeps instead of holding a half-open socket that reads up while forwarding nothing. Positive control, not assertion: the MainPID was killed deliberately and systemd restarted it (NRestarts 0 → 1, listener back, predicate green). THE HOST'S OWN POWEROFF IS NOT THE TUNNEL'S FAULT: the box was powered off at the hypervisor and rebooted 2026-10-24 (boot 12:49), producing a SECOND red episode — UNHEALTHY 12:12:13Z → HEALTHY 12:53:10Z, 41 min — and the unit came back on boot (ActiveEnter 12:52:24, MainPID 730, NRestarts 0 because a boot start is not a crash-restart). So check `who -b` before blaming the tunnel for a red. No new episode since 2026-10-24T12:53:10Z. THE MONTH IS WORSE THAN ANY RETAINED WINDOW SHOWS: endpoint 15 is 8,033 successful of 42,309 executions = 81.01% failure, endpoint 13 (mac-tunnel) 3,322 of 8,467 = 60.77%, endpoint 21 (mac-backup) 15 of 29 = 48.28% — so a retained window reading 104/104 describes the last ~1.7 h, not the month. Anything longer than the retained window reads endpoint_uptimes.

announcements.text: The kernel has OOM-killed this daemon TWICE since 2026-10-24, and the second kill falsifies the earlier "no further kill" clause. Kill 1: 2026-10-24T06:06:44Z, pid 3237387, status=9/KILL, dmesg CONSTRAINT_MEMCG, oom_score_adj=100 — pid 3237387 being the very process an earlier version of this entry called the live MainPID. Kill 2: 2026-10-25T23:32:06Z, journal "A process of this unit has been killed by the OOM killer" then status=9/KILL, Failed with result 'signal', "Consumed 2h 58min 1.757s CPU time, 2.0G memory peak, 2.5G memory swap peak"; restarted 23:32:12Z (MainPID 1091416, NRestarts 1). Between them the unit took five CLEAN stop/starts on 10-25 (18:08:43, 18:39:52, 20:13:45, 20:56:02, 21:35:51) — deliberate restarts, not kills — so a stop/start is not evidence of health. The cap is unchanged: MemoryMax 2,147,483,648 and MemorySwapMax 2,684,354,560, set by a USER drop-in. TWO READ TRAPS, both reproduced: (a) this is a USER unit — `systemctl show opencrabs-ops.service` (system scope) fabricates MainPID=0 / MemoryMax=infinity / ActiveState=inactive for a unit that does not exist at that scope, so any cap read without `systemctl --user` is fiction; (b) `dmesg -T` stamps the same kill 24 s AFTER the journal (06:07:08 vs 06:06:44) because it converts from monotonic with the current offset — it is the wrong instrument for an instant. THE RESERVE IS ONE REMAINDER, not two: the kernel's predicate is current + swap.current >= max + swap.max, so headroom and swap-free are two halves of a single quantity and no single-instant burst/remainder ratio may be quoted. Live at 2026-10-26T06:05:51Z: memory.current 2,046,410,752 of 2,147,483,648 = 95.29% (headroom 96.4 MiB), swap.current 1,362,341,888 of 2,684,354,560 = 50.75% (swap free 1,260.8 MiB), remainder 1,357.2 MiB; memory.peak 2,147,602,432 = 118,784 B OVER max; memory.events low 0 / high 1 / max 72,393 / oom 0 / oom_kill 0 — and those zeros are PER-INCARNATION, so a fresh zero beside a fresh kill is not a clean life. THE WATCHER IS PROVEN END TO END: endpoint 34 logged five UNHEALTHY→HEALTHY pairs on 10-25, the last 23:33:01→23:43:01 matching the kill restart.

announcements.text: The two board/ledger agreement gates are RETIRED, not red. tests/test_close_board_recorded.py and tests/test_board_intake_recorded.py assert a board/ledger close agreement, and this factory's issue board IS its ledger — ONE surface — so the two-surface predicate is INAPPLICABLE rather than failed. They were declared RED BY DESIGN at ledger n=611 and were the only REDs in the 23-gate audit. As of 2026-10-19 they are retired through the KIT'S DECLARED-ABSENT STATE, never by deletion: each reads the declared boundary from docs/ledger-invariants.json, this tree declares none, so each prints a named SKIP ('no docs/ledger-invariants.json — the boundary is a DECLARED factory parameter (#78 clause b)') and STILL RUNS EVERY PROBE — 11 on the close gate, 15 on the intake gate. HOW TO READ THEM NOW: a SKIP is the expected, correct state and is NOT a regression; but a RED from either gate IS a real defect — the retire was built so it cannot disguise a removed or broken gate. The four judgement probes are hermetic (a synthetic tree), and each gate keeps a positive control: a DECLARED boundary must still fail a bad row. The old 'RED BY DESIGN, do not file as a regression' instruction is WITHDRAWN — filing one of these as a regression is now the wrong call only if it SKIPPED; if it FAILED, file it. Owner directive 2026-10-19: 'i don't want to be asked such low level questions any more' — q27 is answered and the class (kit convention, internal mechanics) is now HQ's to decide, never the owner register's. Commits aed7c5af (gates + roles/hq.md + ledger n=1482) and 0c4952eb (prose refs). Full audit after: 24/24 gates PASS.

announcements.text: A Gatus alert page can be SILENTLY LOST: the relay on vpn forwards it over an SSH hop to the agents host's A2A gateway, and when that hop fails the receiver records delivered=false (transport_error) and the target lane is never woken. THIS ENTRY PREVIOUSLY SAID "the owner's q16 ACCEPTS the loss" — that citation is WITHDRAWN as a misattribution, not because the defect healed. q16 is a different question (the notify forward leg's ack-wait budget: "its ack-wait budget has been outgrown twice and its delivered verdict can no longer increment — which shape?"), answered 2026-10-02T12:33:31Z with "Trust the notify queue - the notifications always land. If they are list, it's not a problem" — an assertion that notifications LAND, which is the opposite of an acceptance that one can be lost. So no owner acceptance of page loss exists, and no factory may cite one. The warning stands on its own measurement: do not treat a Gatus page as a guaranteed wake — verify the episode in the receiver's store or the ledger when the alert matters, because a failed forward leaves no trace in the topic it should have woken.

If they are list, it's not a problem" — quoted in full so the next reader can judge the citation rather than inherit it.

THE THREE FALLS ARE ALL EXPLAINED and none was a reap of a profile home: (1) 20G→17G on 10-24: Triage reclaimed an orphaned rsync sender by exact PID, 3.99 GiB (ledger n=1737). (2) 17G→14G on 10-25: the DAEMON incrementally-vacuums its own stores — "incremental_vacuum drained to completion (#321) pages_budget=4096 steps=4096" (src/db/database.rs:578) about every 5 min, 83 times on 10-25 alone. A large freelist is therefore a TRANSIENT state and a disk figure taken mid-drain is not a trend. announcements.text: The cpu controller's delegation to this cgroup is INTERMITTENT, not settled, and a previous version of this entry wrongly recorded it as arrived — read it live, never carry it from a prior round. Measured: ABSENT 2026-10-23T07:23Z (cgroup.controllers 'memory pids', no cpu.max); PRESENT 2026-10-25T18:22:56Z (controllers 'cpu memory pids', cpu.max 'max 100000'); ABSENT AGAIN 2026-10-26T06:05:51Z and re-read 06:10:00Z (controllers 'memory pids', cpu.max -> No such file or directory, app.slice/cgroup.subtree_control 'memory pids'). cpu IS available one level up — app.slice/cgroup.controllers reads 'cpu memory pids' and user@0's subtree_control reads 'cpu memory pids' — so it exists and was simply not delegated down; no app.slice.d drop-in exists in either scope and the journal since 10-25 carries ZERO mentions of the cpu controller or delegation, so the transitions are attributed to no act. WHAT SURVIVES, and is the fact a peer needs: THERE IS NO CEILING IN EFFECT EITHER WAY. When cpu.max exists it reads 'max 100000' (an unlimited quota) with cpu.stat nr_periods 0 / nr_throttled 0 / throttled_usec 0 / nr_bursts 0; CPUQuotaPerSecUSec is infinity; and when cpu.max is absent there is no quota object at all. systemd's stop line for a prior incarnation reads 'Consumed 5h 32min 14.340s CPU time', uncapped. THE LOAD FINDING STANDS and is why this entry exists: host-diag's calibration is a ldavg-15 series, so a load1 peak is NOT comparable with its 12.99 max; on 2026-10-23 load15 sat between p99 8.63 and max 12.99 with disk 87% and MemAvailable 1315 MB both inside their thresholds, making the load leg the SOLE trigger — and the load is the factory's own concurrent gate runs, registry renders and test suites, not a host fault. Steal is a DISTRIBUTION: 11.35% and 23.54% in adjacent windows against a 6.83% lifetime average, sar at native 600 s reading 6.20 / 8.53 / 10.25%, so it rises and falls with our own load — a second cause alongside our work, never a substitute for it. Two /proc/stat windows read busy 98.38% / 99.01%.
